### The Carmel Valley Market, Handled With Care

Carmel Valley condominiums and townhomes offer the rare combination buyers want in North County San Diego: award-winning schools, walkable village centers, coastal proximity, and a lock-and-leave lifestyle.

From the gated enclaves near One Paseo to the established communities of West Carmel Valley and Pacific Highlands Ranch, each has its own character, HOA structure, and price point. Knowing the difference is what separates a good purchase from a great one.

As a Keller Williams Realty agent who has worked these streets for 11+ years, I help buyers and sellers move with confidence — backed by real market data, not guesswork.

*Good to Know*

### Carmel Valley Condo & Townhome FAQs

#### What's the difference between a condo and a townhome here?

In Carmel Valley the distinction is often about ownership structure rather than appearance. Condos typically involve ownership of the interior unit with shared common areas, while townhomes frequently include the land beneath the unit. MLS listings sometimes use the terms interchangeably, so it's worth confirming the specifics of any property — something I help every client sort out.

#### What is the price range for condos and townhomes in Carmel Valley?

Pricing varies by community, size, and age. Entry-level condos typically start in the mid-to-high range for the 92130 zip, while larger townhomes and newer luxury residences near One Paseo command a premium. Reach out for a current, community-specific price breakdown.

#### Are Carmel Valley condos and townhomes a good investment?

Carmel Valley's top-rated schools, coastal access, and steady demand have historically supported strong long-term value. Both condos and townhomes appeal to lifestyle buyers and investors seeking lower-maintenance ownership in a premium San Diego submarket.

#### What do HOA fees typically cover?

Most Carmel Valley HOAs cover exterior maintenance, common-area landscaping, insurance for shared structures, and amenities such as pools or fitness centers. Fees and inclusions differ by community — I can provide the specifics for any community you're considering.

#### How competitive is the Carmel Valley market?

Well-priced condos and townhomes in desirable communities often move quickly. Working with a local specialist who sees new inventory early — and understands each HOA — gives you a meaningful edge.

### Start Your Carmel Valley Search

Whether you're buying your first condo, right-sizing into a townhome, or selling in a competitive market, let's talk strategy. No pressure — just straight answers from someone who knows this market.

*The First Question*

### What a 1-Bed vs. a 2-Bed Actually Costs

Arborlake only comes in two sizes — there's no 3-bedroom floor plan in this community. Here's what each has sold for over the last 5 years, straight from closed MLS sales.

#### 1 Bedroom

6 sales · 5 yrs

- **Size:** 742–896 sq ft
- **Median sale price:** $631,750
- **Price range:** $578K–$815K

#### 2 Bedroom

16 sales · 5 yrs

- **Size:** 964–1,145 sq ft
- **Median sale price:** $800,000
- **Price range:** $675K–$900K

Two-bedrooms have sold nearly three times as often as one-bedrooms — a narrower buyer pool for the smaller units usually means more negotiating room if a 1-bed is what you're after. See the [full 5-year breakdown](https://carmelvalleycondos.com/arborlake-condos-for-sale/#analysis) below for how that gap has moved year to year.

Closed MLS sales, last 5 years.

### About the Arborlake Community

Arborlake is a 190-unit condo community in southwest Carmel Valley, built by Baldwin Homes between 1986 and 1989. What sets it apart from newer 92130 developments is its water-feature setting: a central lake, multiple fountains and waterfalls, and paved walking paths winding through greenbelts that have had nearly four decades to mature.

Units range from 742-square-foot one-bedrooms to 1,145-square-foot two-bedroom layouts, with most patios and balconies oriented toward the lake and landscaping rather than the parking areas. The community sits just north of Carmel View Road and Camino Mira Del Mar — one of the earliest-developed pockets of Carmel Valley, so the surrounding sidewalks, parks, and street trees are as established as the grounds themselves.

As a Keller Williams Realty agent who has worked this community for 11+ years, I can walk you through current HOA details, recent comparable sales, and what to look for in a specific building or floor plan. You can also browse the full [Arborlake community profile](https://www.carmelvalley.com/condos-for-sale/arborlake/) on my Carmel Valley Homes search site.

![Arborlake condominium community in Carmel Valley, San Diego](https://carmelvalleycondos.com/images/arborlake-condos-carmel-valley.jpg)

*What Stands Out*

### Three Reasons Buyers Choose Arborlake

#### The Lake & Water Features

A central lake with multiple fountains and waterfalls runs through the community — a setting no newer, denser 92130 development has room to replicate. Most patios and balconies face the water and landscaping rather than parking.

#### Resort-Style Amenities

Two lighted tennis courts, a heated pool, two spas, a dry sauna, and a fitness center — all HOA-maintained. Few condo communities this age in Carmel Valley still offer this full a recreation package.

#### Mature, Walkable Grounds

Built out between 1986 and 1989, Arborlake's greenbelts and paved walking paths have had nearly four decades to mature — a level of tree canopy and established landscaping that a newly built community simply can't offer yet.

*Before You Buy*

### What to Know Before Buying at Arborlake

The honest tradeoffs, not just the highlights — so there are no surprises at inspection.

#### Carport parking, not a garage

Covered carport parking with storage is included, but it's not an enclosed garage — worth factoring in if that matters for your lifestyle or a second vehicle.

#### Floor plans vary by building

Some units are ground-floor walk-ups, others are upper-level with stairs — confirm the specific floor, elevator access, and layout before falling in love with a listing photo.

#### HOA covers the exterior, not the interior

The ~$408/mo HOA handles building exteriors, the lake, landscaping, and amenities. Interior updates — kitchens, baths, flooring — are the owner's responsibility, so ask about a specific unit's renovation history.

#### No private yard

Like any condo community, outdoor space is a patio or balcony, not a yard. If private outdoor space is a priority, compare unit size and patio orientation carefully — lake-facing units are the most sought after.

*Cost of Ownership*

### What the Arborlake HOA Covers

At roughly $408 per month, Arborlake's HOA runs higher than most comparable southwest Carmel Valley condo communities — here's exactly what that funds.

- Central lake, fountain & waterfall maintenance
- Two lighted tennis courts
- Heated pool and two spas
- Dry sauna and fitness center
- All greenbelt landscaping
- Exterior building maintenance
- Covered carport parking with storage

#### How Arborlake's HOA Compares

- **Arborlake:** ~$408/mo
- **The Lakes:** ~$397/mo
- **Carmel Pointe:** ~$350/mo
- **Del Mar Villas:** ~$340/mo
- **Martinique:** ~$335/mo

Arborlake also carries no Mello-Roos, with a property tax rate around 1.07% — the HOA gap mostly reflects the lake and fountain system the other communities don't have.

#### Five Years of Arborlake Sales: What the Data Shows

Written November 2026 from 22 closed sales (late 2021–2026). The other tabs update automatically.

- **Price per square foot is rising.** It climbed two years running, to about $815/sq ft in 2025 and $833/sq ft in 2026, a steadier signal than the median price.
- **2-bedrooms are the main market.** 16 of the 22 sales were 2-bedrooms. 1-bedrooms sell less often, which usually means more room to negotiate.
- **Well-priced units sell fast again.** 2025 sales averaged 6 days on market, down from 62 days in 2024.

#### The Big Picture: 22 Sales, Six Years

Between late 2021 and today, 22 Arborlake condos have closed escrow. That's not a large sample — some years saw as few as one or two sales, so 2021 and 2024 in particular are single data points, not statistically reliable averages — so the year-by-year numbers in the Overview tab are best read as a trend, not a guarantee. Still, the trend is legible: after a dip through 2022–2023, median prices have climbed in each of the last two full years.

#### Price Per Square Foot Is the Steadier Signal

Median price swings around in a market this small — a single larger or smaller unit selling in a given year can shift the headline number by tens of thousands of dollars. Price per square foot is a cleaner read, because it adjusts for exactly that. And on that measure, Arborlake's story is less bumpy than the median-price table suggests: a climb from $663/sq ft in 2021 to the $770s through 2022–2023, a dip in 2024, and then a clear move upward to $815/sq ft in 2025 and $833/sq ft so far in 2026.

Two consecutive years of rising price per square foot, even while the raw median bounced around, is the more trustworthy signal that Arborlake values are genuinely appreciating — not just that bigger units happened to sell.

#### A Tale of Two Unit Types

Arborlake's 1-bedroom and 2-bedroom units have moved differently enough over the last five years that lumping them into one number hides more than it reveals.

- **2-bed median · 16 sales · $675K–$900K range:** $800,000
- **1-bed median · 6 sales · $578K–$815K range:** $631,750

Two-bedroom units have been the steadier performer: 16 closings, a tight-ish range, and a trend line that points up across the five-year window. One-bedrooms are a different story — only six sales, a wider spread relative to their price point, and a flatter-to-slightly-declining trend. Some of that gap is a sample-size artifact (six sales is not much to draw a line through), but some of it likely reflects genuine demand: two-bedroom units suit a broader range of buyers — downsizers who still want a guest room, small families, investors targeting a wider renter pool — while one-bedrooms draw a narrower, more price-sensitive buyer. The one outlier worth noting: a 1-bedroom sold for $815,000 in the dataset, well above the 1-bed median, almost certainly reflecting an upgraded or larger-than-typical unit rather than a shift in the baseline 1-bed market.

#### Days on Market Tell Their Own Story

If price is what a home sold for, days on market is how hard the seller had to work for it. Arborlake's pattern here is noisy — again, small numbers — but the direction lines up with the price data: 2025's four sales averaged just 6 days on market, among the fastest of the five-year window, while 2024's two sales (one of which sat 79 days) averaged 62. That's consistent with a market that cooled into 2023–2024 and has since tightened back up, rewarding well-priced, well-presented units with quick sales again.

#### How the HOA Fits Into the Value Picture

None of this happens in a vacuum. Arborlake's HOA runs around $408/month — the highest of the nearby comparable communities this page tracks — and that premium buys something those comparables don't have: a maintained central lake with fountains and waterfalls, two tennis courts, a heated pool, two spas, a sauna, and a fitness center. The price and $/sq ft trends in the other tabs suggest the market has been willing to pay for that, not penalize it — appreciation has continued even as the HOA gap versus nearby communities has stayed roughly constant.

#### What This Means If You're Buying or Selling

**If you're buying:** don't anchor too hard to any single closed sale — with this few transactions a year, one unusually large or small unit can swing the "median" meaningfully. Price per square foot and the direction of days-on-market are more reliable signals than any one closing. And know that 2-bedroom units have a longer, steadier sales history to lean on than 1-bedrooms do.

**If you're selling:** the data says pricing discipline matters more now than it did in the slower 2023–2024 stretch. The fastest, highest sales in this dataset — several under 10 days on market in 2025 — went to units priced right and presented well from day one, not to units that started high and chased the market down.

*Find Your Fit*

### Is Arborlake the Right Community for You?

#### Setting-Driven Buyers

If what you see outside your window and hear on a morning walk matters to your decision, Arborlake's lake and mature landscaping aren't matched by comparable 92130 condo communities at this price point.

#### Downsizers

A pool, spa, and sauna a short walk away, zero personal yard maintenance, and grounds that are at their most established right now — four decades in.

#### Investors

Rental demand here is tied to the community's character, and the no-Mello-Roos structure keeps carrying costs predictable for long-term holds.

- Del Mar Highlands Town Center — ~15 min walk
- SR-56 — ~0.6 miles
- Interstate 5 — ~2.5 miles
- Del Mar beaches — ~3.5 miles

*Schools*

### Assigned Schools

- Elementary — Carmel Del Mar Elementary — Del Mar Union Elementary School District
- Middle School — Carmel Valley Middle School — San Dieguito Union High School District
- High School — Torrey Pines High School — San Dieguito Union · among California's top-ranked public high schools
- High School (Alt.) — Canyon Crest Academy — San Dieguito Union · arts & academics magnet

School assignments can change. Verify current boundaries directly with [Del Mar Union SD](https://www.dmusd.org/Page/191) and [San Dieguito Union HSD](https://www.sduhsd.net/about/boundary-maps) before relying on them for a purchase decision.

*Visiting in Person*

### What to Check When You Tour Arborlake

Five things worth inspecting or asking about on a showing — bring this list.

- **Which way the unit faces** — Ask whether the patio or balcony faces the lake and landscaping, or the parking and carports — it's the single biggest value driver within the community.
- **Floor level and stairs** — Confirm whether it's a ground-floor walk-up or an upper unit with stairs, and ask about elevator access for that specific building — it matters for daily life and resale.
- **Noise from the amenities** — Units near the tennis courts or pool can pick up activity noise on weekends — worth a visit at a busy time if that matters to you.
- **Age of interior systems** — The buildings date to 1986–1989. Ask the seller's agent for the age of the water heater, HVAC, and any plumbing updates specific to that unit.
- **Assigned carport and storage** — Confirm which carport space and storage unit convey with the home, and how close they are to the actual front door — this varies by building.

*Good to Know*

### Arborlake Condo FAQs

#### What is the price range for Arborlake condos?

Arborlake condos typically sell between $650,000 and $875,000, or roughly $680–$820 per square foot depending on the unit's condition and position within the community.

#### What do Arborlake HOA fees cover?

Arborlake's HOA runs approximately $408 per month and covers the community's central lake and fountain system, two lighted tennis courts, a heated pool, two spas, a dry sauna, a fitness center, all greenbelt landscaping, exterior building maintenance, and covered carport parking with storage.

#### Does Arborlake have Mello-Roos?

No — Arborlake carries no Mello-Roos assessment, with a property tax rate of approximately 1.07% of assessed value.

#### How big are the units at Arborlake?

Arborlake units range from 742-square-foot one-bedrooms to 1,145-square-foot two-bedroom layouts.

#### How does Arborlake compare to other Carmel Valley condo communities?

Arborlake's HOA runs higher than comparable communities like The Lakes (~$397/mo), Carmel Pointe (~$350/mo), and Del Mar Villas (~$340/mo) — the difference mostly funds the central lake, fountains, and waterfalls that those communities don't have.

#### How quickly do Arborlake condos sell?

Well-priced, updated listings typically go under contract within 2–3 weeks, reflecting a buyer pool that often targets this specific community rather than comparison-shopping broadly.

### Where Condo & Townhome Prices Stand

- $815 · Price / Sq Ft · Average, 2026 year to date

*2022 – 2026*

### Condo & Townhome Prices by Year

Closed condo and townhome sales in Carmel Valley San Diego 92130, by calendar year.

| Year | Homes Sold | Median Sale Price | Avg. Price / Sq Ft | Avg. Days on Market | Sale vs. Original List |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 (Jan 1 – Oct 22) | 98 | $995,000 | $815 | 32 | 97.9% |
| 2025 | 151 | $970,000 | $815 | 30 | 98.4% |
| 2024 | 143 | $970,000 | $838 | 19 | 100.0% |
| 2023 | 139 | $969,000 | $790 | 28 | 100.0% |
| 2022 | 180 | $942,500 | $799 | 16 | 102.2% |

Condos and townhomes are reported together as attached homes, since listing agents frequently enter a townhome as a condo — or the reverse — in the MLS. Source: closed sales reported in the MLS for zip code 92130, January 3, 2022 – October 22, 2026, compiled by Sez Sezer, Keller Williams Realty. 2026 is year to date.

*What It Means*

### Reading the Carmel Valley Condo Market

#### For Buyers

The median condo and townhome price has climbed from $942,500 in 2022 to $995,000 year to date in 2026 — a gain of roughly 5.6% over five years, far steadier than the swings seen in detached single-family homes over the same stretch. Days on market in 2026 sit at 32, up from the 16-19 day pace of 2022-2024, giving buyers a bit more room to evaluate HOA financials and unit condition before competing.

#### For Sellers

Price per square foot has held in the high-$700s to low-$800s range every year since 2022, with 2026 pricing right in line with 2025. Units are still selling close to original list price — 97.9% to 100% most years — which means overpricing, not a soft market, is the main thing costing sellers time on market. A well-priced, well-presented condo in an established Carmel Valley community is still moving in roughly a month or less.

*Good to Know*

### Market Report FAQ

#### What is the median price for a condo or townhome in Carmel Valley?

The median sale price for Carmel Valley condos and townhomes in 92130 is $995,000 year to date in 2026, based on 98 closed sales, up from a median of $970,000 in 2025.

#### Why are condos and townhomes reported together?

Listing agents frequently enter a townhome as a condo in the MLS, or the reverse, so the two property types are reported together as "attached homes" to keep the year-over-year data consistent and accurate.

#### How fast are Carmel Valley condos selling right now?

Condos and townhomes averaged 32 days on market in 2026 year to date, up slightly from 2024's 19-day average, but still selling at 97.9% of original list price — a sign that well-priced units continue to move efficiently.

#### Is now a good time to buy or sell a Carmel Valley condo?

Prices have risen steadily and days on market remain reasonable by historical standards, which tends to favor sellers who price accurately and buyers who are prepared to move quickly on well-presented units. The right strategy depends on your specific community and timeline — reach out for a tailored read on your situation.
